versions.body:
# Postmortem: discrepancy in a plugin entry point change

This window originally covered only recording changes to the plugin's public entry points. The visible outcome during the window did not match the original plan: the retained entry point and the entry point actually observed were different. This was not initially treated as a runtime issue; the team on site first handled it as an omission in the change record. That assessment applied only to what was observed at the time and did not explain why the same input produced different results.

### Timeline

- By the time the discrepancy was first noticed, the change was already in the window. The checkpoint covered only the planned replacement entry point and did not retain the old package entry point for a side-by-side check.
- The same input frame sequence was then replayed. The records showed that the visible outcome still differed, but the records themselves did not establish whether the discrepancy occurred during recording, packaging, or loading.
- During the investigation, the team looked back once using `src/three/plugins/CesiumIonAuthPlugin.js` and the call names. That location helped narrow the search, but this does not establish it as the point of failure.
- To keep the window's impact from spreading further, the team on site restored the retained old package entry point. After the restore, the new entry point in the original plan was no longer considered available for this window.

The main impact was on the visibility of public entry point change records, rather than confirmed breakage in the plugin implementation. Since the old entry point remained usable, replacement was not pursued further in the window. However, colleagues relying on the records to confirm the entry point would see a package surface different from the original plan and needed to be told separately that a temporary restore had taken place.

### Controls added at the time

Three requirements were later added to the window record: the old package entry point must be retained during the change; replacement must stop if the visible outcome does not match the record; and the rollback steps must be executable independently by the person on duty, without relying on their memory of verbal arrangements from the previous round. Here, "stop" means stopping the entry point replacement, not claiming that the root cause has been found.

The provisional conclusion at the time was that, as an initial step, it would be enough to put public entry point recording and package surface verification into the same window check. That statement is retained here because it guided the restore; it did not address the source of the discrepancy in the same input frame sequence, nor did it prove that all future entry point changes would encounter the same kind of problem.

### Still unconfirmed

It has not yet been established whether the discrepancy first arose in the recorded details, in the generated package, or because a different entry point was selected at load time. The restore only brought the visible outcome back to the old package entry point; it did not establish the root cause. If another window of this kind is opened later, records that can distinguish these three stages should be obtained first, before deciding whether to attempt the replacement again.

### Evidence collection order for the next window

Before starting another replacement, first save the recorded details and the package surface to be released side by side, then use the same input frame sequence to record the entry point actually selected on the loading side. Keep a timestamp for each of the three records; do not use post-restore results to backfill the initial discovery. If the three still cannot be reconciled, stop the entry point replacement and keep the old package usable; the person on duty is to record only the unknowns, not describe the temporary restore as a root-cause fix.

The review record should also state separately who performed the restore, whether it depended on other changes within the window, and which entry point ordinary callers actually saw after the restore. If any item is missing, keep the window on hold and start a separate record for further investigation. This sequence is only for distinguishing between recording, generation, and loading; it does not change the conclusion of this postmortem or show that a failure has already occurred at any of these stages.

The controls added this time were "retaining the old package entry point during the change window, stop conditions, and rollback steps that can be executed independently"; the record will not be rewritten to imply that the root cause was already known at the time of the restore.
